title: Watch delta
description: What one run of a standing site watch found new since the last run (`umbra_py.watch.WatchResult.to_dict`), emitted by `umbra watch --json`. This is the document a *scheduler* reads: the run is idempotent and involves no model call, so the same query run twice reports the second time only what arrived in between. `new_count` of zero is the normal case and the one a cron job should stay quiet about.

watch.description: The watch's name — the key its state is stored under. Derived from the query when the caller names none (a legible slug plus a short hash of the normalized filters), so the same query always lines up on the same stored state and two different queries essentially never collide.

checked_at.description: The date this run was made, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`.

first_run.description: True when the watch had no stored state before this run, which is when `new_items` is the whole current selection rather than a delta. A scheduler should treat a first run as a baseline rather than as news.

new_count.description: How many acquisitions are new (the length of `new_items`).

total_seen.description: The size of the watch's state after this run — the running count of distinct acquisitions it has ever reported.

query.description: A JSON echo of the search that produced the delta, so a stored result says what it was watching. Unset filters are dropped rather than emitted as nulls, which is why this object is open rather than a fixed key set: it carries whichever of `area` / `place` / `bbox` / `intersects` / `product_types` / `start` / `end` / `fuzzy` / `limit` the run actually used.

new_items.description: The new acquisitions, each as a full context card rather than an id — so the next step (download, describe, stack) needs no second fetch to act on one.

attribution.description: The attribution line, carried here as on every data-bearing surface in the library.
